model_output.verdict: A computer science graduate with relevant projects and an internship whose contributions need more detail.
write_up: You’re a computer science graduate aiming for Software Engineer roles, with a Cardinal Health internship, help desk experience and three programming projects. It’s common for an early-career resume to lean on duties, but yours won’t stand out in a pile when a recruiter can’t tell which features, tests or fixes were yours at Cardinal Health.

Your Personal Finance Tracker line is a good model: it names the application, what it does and the tools you used. Education sits above Experience even though you have more than a year of work history. Moving Experience up gives the internship and help desk work an earlier look.

Let’s start with the Cardinal Health internship. Replace the general lines with the features you developed, the tests you wrote and the bugs you fixed. Then add a little more about the help desk tickets, and keep the project details that already show what you built.

cards.line: Motivated and detail-oriented Computer Science graduate seeking a Software Engineer position where I can leverage my technical skills and passion for problem solving to contribute to a dynamic team.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the job you want, but the description could fit almost any graduate. Your internship gives you a more distinctive introduction.
cards.example: Computer Science graduate seeking a Software Engineer position, with experience developing an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot.
cards.question: Which part of your internship would you most want a recruiter to notice first?

cards.line: Education sits above Experience.
cards.cannot_tell: Your internship and help desk work come after coursework and skills. With more than a year of work history, put Experience first so a recruiter reaches that work sooner.
cards.question: Can you move Experience above Education while keeping your degree and graduation date easy to find?

cards.line: - Responsible for developing features for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot
cards.cannot_tell: The application and tools are clear, but the features aren't. A recruiter needs to know what you developed.
cards.example: Developed [features] for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot.
cards.question: Which features did you develop for the inventory application?

cards.line: - Participated in daily stand-ups and sprint planning meetings as part of an Agile team
cards.cannot_tell: Meetings show how the team worked, not what you contributed. Use this space for a piece of work that came out of a sprint.
cards.example: Participated in sprint planning as part of an Agile team and contributed [work completed] during [sprint].
cards.question: What work did you contribute during a sprint?

cards.line: - Wrote unit tests to improve code quality and reliability
cards.cannot_tell: Unit tests are useful work, but a recruiter can't tell what they covered. Name the functionality you tested.
cards.example: Wrote unit tests for [functionality] to improve code quality and reliability.
cards.question: What functionality did your unit tests cover?

cards.line: - Collaborated with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver solutions
cards.cannot_tell: The teams, requirements and solutions are all unnamed. One example would show what you worked on with other people.
cards.example: Collaborated with [teams] to gather requirements for [need] and deliver [solution].
cards.question: Which teams did you work with, and what requirement and solution did you contribute to?

cards.line: - Fixed bugs and performed code reviews
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell what you fixed or what code you reviewed. Pick an example that shows the work behind those tasks.
cards.example: Fixed [bugs] and performed code reviews for [code or features].
cards.question: Which bugs did you fix, and what code or features did you review?

cards.line: - Resolved tickets in a timely manner and documented solutions
cards.cannot_tell: Tickets and documented solutions are relevant to support work, but their volume and subject are missing. Those details would show what the job involved.
cards.example: Resolved [number] tickets [time period] involving [issues] and documented solutions.
cards.question: What kinds of tickets did you resolve, and how many did you typically handle over a given period?

cards.line: - Built a Python application to track expenses and visualize spending with matplotlib
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives a recruiter a concrete thing you built and its purpose without relying on a list of responsibilities.

fit.note: Your internship and projects point toward entry-level software engineering, particularly web application work. The projects show what you built; the internship needs more detail about your individual contributions.
